blocks.text: The Clearing Corporation (e.g., NSCCL for NSE) acts as the central counterparty to all trades. It guarantees that every trade will be settled, eliminating counterparty risk.
Novation: The legal process where the Clearing Corporation replaces the original buyer and seller to become the buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer.
Not everyone can clear trades. Members are categorized based on their rights:

items: Trading Member (TM): Can trade for themselves and clients but CANNOT clear/settle trades. They must link to a Clearing Member.
Trading cum Clearing Member (TCM): Can trade and clear their own trades and their clients' trades.
Professional Clearing Member (PCM): They do not trade but only clear and settle trades for other Trading Members (usually Banks/Custodians).

blocks.text: Margins are funds collected by the exchange to cover potential losses. This is the backbone of risk management.

items: Initial Margin (SPAN): Calculated based on volatility (worst-case loss in 1 day). Must be paid BEFORE trading.
Extreme Loss Margin (ELM): A fixed percentage collected over and above SPAN margin to cover extreme situations.
Calendar Spread Margin: Lower margin benefit given when you buy one month and sell another month.

blocks.text: MTM is the process of adjusting the daily profits and losses. If you make a loss today, you must pay it to the exchange immediately.
Critical Rule: MTM losses must be paid in CASH by the next working day (T+1). Initial margins can be non-cash (securities/FDs), but MTM is always cash.
